summary: Stephan Beyer worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, having studied under Richard Hugh Robinson. He served as a professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (attested 1977).
Stephan Marcus Salzberg specializes in Sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of British Columbia (attested 1983) under Yoshitaka Iriya, Shoko Kanaoka, and Daniel L. Overmyer.

Stephanie Kaza studied at Oberlin College, Stanford University, the Starr King School for the Ministry, and the University of California, Santa Cruz. A scholar of religious and Buddhist studies, she served as Professor of Environmental Studies at the University of Vermont (~1991–2015).
Stephanie Roemer is a Tibetologist who completed her doctoral studies under supervisors Eberhard Sandschneider and Toni Huber.

Stephanie W. Jamison, a scholar of Indology and linguistics, studied at Yale University (~1973–1977). She held positions at Harvard University (~1986–1992, attested 2004) and became Professor of Sanskrit and Indo-Iranian Linguistics at UCLA around 2002.

Stephen Addiss (1935–2022) worked in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology, earning his Ph.D. from the University of Michigan (~1971–1977). He was a professor of art history at the University of Kansas (~1977–1992) and taught at the University of Richmond (~1992–2013).

Stephen Batchelor is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under traditional teachers Ngawang Dhargyey (~1972–1974), Geshe Rabten (~1974–1980), and Kusan Sunim (~1981–1984). He held a post at Songgwangsa from 1981 to 1984.

Stephen C. Berkwitz specializes in religious and Buddhist studies. He held a Fulbright Junior Fellowship at the University of Kelaniya (1995–1997) and has served as Associate Professor of Religious Studies at Missouri State University.

Stephen F. Teiser studied at Oberlin College (~1974–1978) and earned his PhD at Princeton University (~1980–1986). A scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies, he taught at Middlebury College (~1986–1988) before becoming D.T. Suzuki Professor at Princeton (~1996).

Stephen G. Covell is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He completed his doctoral studies under Jacqueline I. Stone at Princeton University (~1995–2001) and joined Western Michigan University around 2003.

Stephen H. West, a Sinologist, studied at National Taiwan Normal University and the University of Michigan (~1966–1972). He served as Professor of East Asian Languages at UC Berkeley (~1986–2003) and held a post at Arizona State University (~2003–2016).

Stephen J. Laumakis works in philosophy and Buddhist studies, having studied under John Kronen, Ramdas Lamb, and George J. Tanabe, Jr. He served as Professor of Philosophy and Director of the Aquinas Scholars Honors Program at the University of St. Thomas (attested 2013).

Stephen L. Jenkins (1953–2016) worked in Buddhist and religious studies, completing doctoral studies at Harvard under Masatoshi Nagatomi and Charles Hallisey. He served as Professor of Religious Studies at California State Polytechnic University, Humboldt (attested 2010–2013).
Stephen Prothero is a scholar of religious studies who studied at Yale University (~1978–1982) and Harvard University (~1985–1990). He joined Boston University around 1996.

Stephen R. Bokenkamp studied at UC Berkeley (~1978–1986). Working in Sinology and religious studies, he served as Associate Professor of Classical Chinese at Indiana University (~1986–2007) and became Professor of Chinese at Arizona State University around 2007.
Stephen Suen specializes in Buddhist studies and earned his PhD at the University of Hong Kong under the supervision of K. L. Dhammajoti (attested 2009).

Steve Odin studied under David A. Dilworth and Edward S. Casey at Stony Brook University (~1976–1980). A specialist in philosophy and Japanology, he was appointed Professor of Philosophy at the University of Hawaii in 1982.

Steven Collins (1950–2018) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed his D.Phil. at Oxford under Richard Gombrich (~1974–1979). He taught at the University of Bristol (~1980–1991) and was the Chester D. Tripp Professor at the University of Chicago (1991).

Steven Edward Lindquist specializes in Indology and religious studies. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Texas at Austin under Patrick Olivelle (attested 2005) and held a post at Concordia University.

Steven Heine, a specialist in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies, studied at the University of Pennsylvania (~1968–1972) and Temple University (~1974–1980). He held posts at Penn State (~1988–1997) and Florida International University (professor, ~1997).
